answer: Forced Divergence Ledger. Each identity must, at random intervals, submit a fresh observation drawn from its own persistent private state (a seeded wander trail) and a signed timestamp; the ledger cross-checks that consecutive entries form a continuous, non-repeating path. Duplicates sharing one underlying state produce correlated paths that a falcon scan detects as duplicated nectar signatures. An attacker cloning an agent pays full compute and storage per clone to maintain divergent state, plus the cost of any single collision exposing the entire cluster.
